blocks.content: A volcano is an opening in the Earth's crust through which molten rock, gases, ash, and fragmented material are expelled onto the surface. Volcanism is closely linked with plate tectonics and mantle processes, making it one of the most important topics in physical geography.
A volcano is an opening in the Earth's crust through which molten rock, gases, ash, and fragmented material are expelled onto the surface.

items: Exams often ask about the drivers of volcanism: remember it is directly linked with plate tectonics and mantle processes.
Be prepared to identify materials expelled during an eruption, which include molten rock, gases, ash, and fragmented material.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A volcano is a vent or opening in the Earth's crust through which materials are expelled onto the surface.
Expelled substances include molten rock, atmospheric gases, volcanic ash, and fragmented rock debris.
Volcanic activity is directly driven by internal mantle processes and the movement of tectonic plates.
